source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which is a goal of palliative care?
questions.rationale: Palliative care is total care. It relieves pain and other distressing symptoms, supports the client to live as actively as possible, and neither hastens nor delays death.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q91 (PDF p. 239)
questions.quote: Palliative care is a philosophy of total care.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which respiratory finding suggests that death is imminent?
questions.rationale: Imminent death shows poor gas exchange (dyspnea, cyanosis) and altered breathing such as slow, labored, irregular, or Cheyne-Stokes respiration.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q154 (PDF p. 304)
questions.quote: altered patterns of respiration, such as slow, labored, irregular, or Cheyne- Stokes pattern

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which is a NORMAL age-related concern when planning care for an older client?
questions.rationale: Older clients are at risk for dehydration, immobility complications, and loss of skin integrity. Incontinence, depression, and confusion are not normal aging.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q171 (PDF p. 324)
questions.quote: Older clients are at risk for dehydration and complications related to immobility.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which eye finding is a normal age-related change?
questions.rationale: Aging brings a flatter cornea (blurred vision), poor adaptation to darkness, yellowing sclera, fewer tears, and poorer color discrimination.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q612 (PDF p. 825)
questions.quote: poor pupillary adaptation to darkness

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which factor increases an older adult's risk for hypothermia?
questions.rationale: Older adults' median oral temperature is about 36°C. Poor thermoregulation, anemia, alcohol, hypoglycemia, and burns raise hypothermia risk.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q620 (PDF p. 835)
questions.quote: Numerous factors increase the risk of hypothermia

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A deceased client will donate his eyes. What care is usually prescribed?
options: Saline gauze and a small ice pack
questions.rationale: The eyes are closed and covered with saline-moistened gauze and a small ice pack. Enucleation follows within 2 to 4 hours.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q458 (PDF p. 640)
questions.quote: placing gauze pads wet with saline over them with a small ice pack

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which finding is a contraindication to organ donation?
questions.rationale: A donor with hepatitis B could infect the recipient. Allergies and travel history are not contraindications.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q594 (PDF p. 802)
questions.quote: A decedent who had a hepatitis B infection cannot donate organs

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which finding shows a brain-dead organ donor is being maintained to standard?
questions.rationale: Urine output of 100 mL/hr shows good renal perfusion. A pH of 7.32 is acidosis and a 5-second refill is too slow.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q595 (PDF p. 803)
questions.quote: Urine output at 100 mL per hour indicates adequate renal perfusion

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: After aggressive cerebral edema treatment, what is the PRIORITY to keep a donor's kidneys viable?
questions.rationale: Kidneys need about 80 mm Hg perfusion pressure. Cerebral edema treatment causes fluid deficit, so volume is restored first.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q596 (PDF p. 804)
questions.quote: The kidneys require a minimum perfusion pressure of 80 mm Hg to produce urine

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which hospital safety measure is specific to infants and toddlers?
questions.rationale: Crib sides are never left down. Large, soft toys without small parts prevent choking.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q475 (PDF p. 659)
questions.quote: crib sides should never be left down because the child could roll and fall.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which statement about preventing burns in a toddler needs MORE teaching?
options: 'I'll put my coffee on the counter.'
questions.rationale: Toddlers can reach hot objects on counters. Hot drinks must be kept out of reach.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q503 (PDF p. 697)
questions.quote: can reach hot water or hot objects placed on counters

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: With which liquid should an adolescent take oral iron?
questions.rationale: Vitamin C enhances iron absorption, and tomato juice is rich in it.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q611 (PDF p. 824)
questions.quote: Iron should be administered with vitamin C–rich fluids

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A crying toddler won't sit still for an eye exam. What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: Involving the toddler in the exam reduces fear. Telling a child not to be scared tells him how to feel.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q682 (PDF p. 902)
questions.quote: Fears in this age group can be decreased by getting the child actively involved in the examination.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A 6-year-old starts bedwetting after a new baby arrives. Which defense mechanism is this?
questions.rationale: Regression is returning to an earlier form of behavior under stress.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q851 (PDF p. 1088)
questions.quote: The defense mechanism of regression is characterized by returning to an earlier form of expressing an impulse.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A preschooler in traction starts bedwetting. How should the nurse explain this to the mother?
questions.rationale: Regression is common in immobilized children and usually needs no professional intervention.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q873 (PDF p. 1110)
questions.quote: Regressive behaviors are not uncommon in immobilized children

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which adolescent statement needs follow-up?
options: 'I like to be alone when stressed.'
'I've cut out all fat and lost weight.'
questions.rationale: Omitting all fat and losing weight during growth suggests poor nutrition and a possible eating disorder.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q852 (PDF p. 1089)
questions.quote: suggests inadequate nutrition and a possible eating disorder.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: How should the nurse prepare an 11-year-old for an IV insertion?
options: Use visual aids and concrete words
questions.rationale: School-age children understand best with visual aids and concrete language.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q860 (PDF p. 1097)
questions.quote: The school-age child understands best with visual aids and concrete language.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which statement by a hospitalized 16-year-old suggests a developmental problem?
questions.rationale: Adolescents who withdraw from peers struggle with identity development.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q867 (PDF p. 1104)
questions.quote: Adolescents who withdraw from peers into isolation struggle with developing identity

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A 9-year-old is in traction for 2 months. What BEST promotes psychosocial development?
questions.rationale: School-age children face industry versus inferiority. Keeping up with schoolwork gives accomplishment.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q939 (PDF p. 1183)
questions.quote: The developmental task of the school-age child is industry versus inferiority.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A 16-year-old with diabetes says, 'I'm fed up with diets and doctors!' What is the PRIORITY concern?
questions.rationale: Adolescents strive for identity and independence; the statement reflects fear of losing control.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q944 (PDF p. 1189)
questions.quote: the situation describes a common fear of loss of control.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which finding in a 12-year-old suggests disrupted self-concept development?
questions.rationale: Intimate relationships are expected in young adulthood. Friends and industry fit this age.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q962 (PDF p. 1209)
questions.quote: The formation of an intimate relationship would not be expected until young adulthood.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which question BEST assesses a teenager's feelings about using a cane?
options: 'How do you feel about the cane?'
questions.rationale: An open-ended question about feelings elicits assessment data. The others are closed or assume feelings.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1043 (PDF p. 1317)
questions.quote: posing an open-ended question to elicit assessment data

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A 14-year-old in skeletal traction struggles with the long stay. What helps MOST?
questions.rationale: Adolescents need to belong to a peer group. Wearing their own clothes supports this.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1202 (PDF p. 1494)
questions.quote: The child should be allowed to wear his or her own clothes to feel a sense of belonging to the group.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A 10-month-old is hospitalized for RSV. Which plan fits his development?
questions.rationale: Infants are in trust versus mistrust. A consistent routine with comfort, touch, and talking supports trust.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1163 (PDF p. 1450)
questions.quote: A 10-month-old infant is in the trust versus mistrust stage of psychosocial development

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which behavior shows a preschooler with scarlet fever is coping with bed rest?
questions.rationale: Play is how preschoolers adjust to life experiences; quiet play like drawing suits bed rest.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1219 (PDF p. 1512)
questions.quote: for the preschooler, play is the best way for children to understand and adjust to life’s experiences.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which outcome shows a positive DEVELOPMENTAL result for a preschooler in traction?
questions.rationale: Hospitalization and immobility may cause regression. Age-appropriate behavior is the developmental outcome.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1232 (PDF p. 1525)
questions.quote: a positive outcome of age-appropriate behavior can be achieved.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which parent statement about toddler temper tantrums shows understanding?
options: 'I'll say only bad kids do it.'
questions.rationale: Ignoring attention-seeking behavior extinguishes it, provided the child is safe. Time-out should be about 1 minute per year of age.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1241 (PDF p. 1534)
questions.quote: Ignoring a negative attention-seeking behavior is considered the best way to extinguish it

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which diabetes task suits a newly diagnosed 9-year-old?
questions.rationale: School-age children can draw up and give insulin with supervision but lack maturity for independent dosing decisions.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1252 (PDF p. 1552)
questions.quote: School-age children have the cognitive and motor skills to draw up and administer insulin with adult supervision.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: At what age can most children begin to monitor their own insulin needs?
questions.rationale: Most children 9 years or older understand the principles of monitoring their insulin needs.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1080 (PDF p. 1362)
questions.quote: Most children 9 years old or older can understand the principles of monitoring their own insulin requirements.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: What should the nurse do FIRST before teaching a teenager about sexuality?
questions.rationale: Establishing a relationship and exploring prior knowledge comes first; it builds rapport and identifies learning needs.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q753 (PDF p. 982)
questions.quote: The first step in effective communication is establishing a relationship.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: What should the nurse assess about a dying client's end-of-life wishes?
questions.rationale: End-of-life assessment includes the preferred place of death, expectations for nursing care, and wishes about comfort and spiritual care.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q741 (PDF p. 967)
questions.quote: End-of-life assessment related to nursing care should include the preferred place for death

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A spouse says, 'I can't keep watching her die.' What is the MOST therapeutic reply?
questions.rationale: An empathetic response acknowledges the spouse's pain and suggests time for self-care.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q816 (PDF p. 1050)
questions.quote: The most therapeutic response is the one that is empathetic

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A dying client says, 'I hope I'm worthy of heaven,' and shows fear. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Assess the nature of the fear
questions.rationale: Fear ranges from mild to overwhelming, so the nurse first assesses its nature, then helps the client express it.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q849 (PDF p. 1086)
questions.quote: the nurse would first assess the nature of the client’s fears

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which behavior shows ANTICIPATORY grieving in a dying client?
questions.rationale: Discussing thoughts and feelings about the loss shows anticipatory grief. The others suggest dysfunctional grieving.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q900 (PDF p. 1143)
questions.quote: The remaining options are examples of dysfunctional grieving.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A dying client is angry that her family keeps hoping for a cure. Which response uses reflection?
questions.rationale: Reflection directs the client's feelings back to validate them.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q925 (PDF p. 1169)
questions.quote: Reflection is the therapeutic communication technique that redirects the client’s feelings back at the client

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which statement shows a dying client has reached ACCEPTANCE?
options: 'I want my family here when I die.'
'When my kids graduate, I'll be ready.'
questions.rationale: Acceptance is often shown by plans for death and wanting loved ones near. The others are bargaining.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q948 (PDF p. 1193)
questions.quote: Acceptance is often characterized by plans for death.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: How can the nurse BEST help a family cope as death nears?
questions.rationale: Open, clear communication helps decision-making and coping and preserves the family's sense of control.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1015 (PDF p. 1288)
questions.quote: Maintaining effective and open communication among family members affected by death and grief is important

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which event BEST shows a client died with dignity?
questions.rationale: The family's response gives external validation that comprehensive, quality care was given.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1021 (PDF p. 1294)
questions.quote: The correct option provides external validation that the client received comprehensive, quality care.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which statement to parents of a stillborn baby shows effective teaching of a new nurse?
options: 'How can I help you remember your baby?'
'I don't know why this happened either.'
questions.rationale: Helping the family create memories confirms the baby's existence and helps them complete grieving.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1024 (PDF p. 1297)
questions.quote: assist the family with creating memories of the infant

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Right after a death, the family refuses to discuss funeral plans. What should the nurse do?
options: Offer time alone with the client
questions.rationale: The family is in denial, the first stage. Offering time alone supports them as they process the death.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1029 (PDF p. 1302)
questions.quote: The family is exhibiting the first stage of grief: denial.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which reaction by the partner of a dying client is an EXPECTED coping response?
questions.rationale: Anger is a normal response to impending loss and is often directed at God, the dying person, or caregivers.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1030 (PDF p. 1303)
questions.quote: The expression of anger is a normal response to impending loss
